blocks.text: Modern commercial and industrial facilities depend on increasingly sophisticated electrical equipment. Variable frequency drives, UPS systems, solar inverters, LED lighting, data-centre equipment, and other power-electronic loads can introduce harmonic distortion into an electrical network. This is why Harmonic Studies in UAE are an important part of electrical system design, power-quality assessment, and troubleshooting. A detailed harmonic study helps engineers understand distortion levels, identify potential risks, and determine suitable mitigation measures before power-quality problems affect equipment or operations.
What Is a Harmonic Study?

A harmonic study is an engineering analysis used to evaluate harmonic currents and voltages within an electrical power system. Ideally, an AC voltage or current waveform follows a clean sinusoidal shape. Non-linear electrical loads can distort this waveform by generating harmonic components at multiples of the fundamental frequency. In the UAE, DEWA’s electrical installation regulations identify several potential sources of harmonics, including variable speed drives, variable frequency drives, capacitor banks, UPS systems, lighting equipment, and electronic power supplies. A harmonic study examines how these sources affect the electrical network and whether the resulting distortion remains within applicable power-quality requirements.

DEWA regulations state that consumer loads should not cause supply-voltage characteristics to deviate beyond applicable requirements, including referenced standards such as BS EN 50160, IEC 61000, and ENA Engineering Recommendation G5/4-1.
What Causes Harmonics in Electrical Systems?
Harmonics are commonly associated with non-linear loads. Typical sources include:
Variable Frequency Drives
VFDs are widely used for controlling motors and improving energy efficiency. However, conventional drive configurations can produce harmonic currents that affect the upstream electrical network.
UPS Systems
UPS equipment protects critical loads from power interruptions, but its rectifier and power-electronic components can contribute to harmonic distortion depending on the system design.
Solar PV Inverters

Solar power systems use inverters to convert DC electricity into AC power. Harmonic performance therefore needs to be considered when connecting larger systems to the electrical network. DEWA has specific harmonic-assessment procedures for Shams Dubai projects, including assessment of harmonic emissions from solar designs.
LED and Electronic Lighting
Modern lighting systems often use electronic drivers that can contribute to harmonic currents.
Data Centres and IT Equipment

Servers, computers, networking equipment, and other electronic loads can create non-linear current demand and increase harmonic distortion within a facility. What Does a Harmonic Study Include? A professional Harmonic Studies in UAE assessment may include several stages.

2. Harmonic Measurement

Where an existing facility is being investigated, power-quality analysers can be used to measure voltage and current harmonics. Measurements may include individual harmonic orders, total harmonic distortion, voltage levels, current levels, power factor, and other relevant power-quality parameters.
3. Electrical System Modelling
The electrical network can then be represented using appropriate power-system analysis software. Engineers can evaluate the behaviour of the system under different operating conditions.
4. Harmonic Analysis

The study evaluates harmonic distortion at important points within the network, such as transformers, main switchboards, distribution boards, and points of common coupling. The analysis can help determine whether harmonic levels could create operational or compliance concerns.

Harmonic Studies and DEWA Requirements

Power quality is an important consideration when connecting electrical installations and distributed renewable-energy systems to the Dubai network. DEWA’s current Distributed Renewable Resources Generators standards specify harmonic and interharmonic considerations for LV and MV connections. For MV-connected renewable systems, DEWA references IEC/TR 61000-3-6 for harmonics and interharmonics and performs a special harmonic evaluation at the network assessment stage. DEWA’s current standards also state that, unless otherwise specified, supply-voltage THD should be no more than 8% for LV networks and 6.5% for MV networks in the referenced context. These requirements demonstrate why harmonic analysis should be considered during electrical design rather than only after a power-quality problem occurs.

Choose the Right Approach to Power Quality

As UAE facilities adopt more automation, renewable energy, digital equipment, and power-electronic systems, understanding harmonic behaviour is becoming increasingly important. Harmonic Studies in UAE provide a structured way to evaluate electrical-system distortion, identify potential risks, and develop appropriate mitigation strategies. Whether you are designing a new facility, upgrading an existing electrical network, or investigating power-quality problems, a detailed harmonic assessment can support safer, more reliable, and more efficient electrical operation.
